subject: Plan options: tier swap + feature bundling for Altomed
messages:
From: David Liao <david.liao@altomed.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring a lower-cost plan + keep X features

Hi Kimberly,

We are re-running our budget for H2 and are evaluating whether we can move off the Current Core tier to something smaller without losing the latency guarantees and a couple of features (prefix caching and per-route tracing). Our usage for inference tokens has dropped ~18% QoQ, but the team still needs stable p95 latency < 350ms for user-facing flows.

Questions:
- Can we move to the Compact tier and add the prefix caching bundle as an add-on?
- If we downgrade, are there easy rollback paths (e.g., pin to a model/version) to recover performance quickly?
- Any options for an introductory concession or one-time credit to offset migration friction?

We also have procurement looped (procurement@altomed.com) — they’ll want clear artifact(s) for the SOW and the pricing grid.

Thanks — happy to hop on 30m if easier.

David
Director, AI Platform
Altomed Health
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-23T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Exploring a lower-cost plan + keep X features

Ben / Marissa — forwarding David's ask. Key asks: downgrade from Core -> Compact but keep prefix caching and per-route tracing; maintain p95 < 350ms; request for concession/credit and SOW/pricing artifacts.

My thoughts:
- Option A: Compact + caching add-on + regional burst (short term) — wins on price but may require aggressive batching/kv tweaks to hit p95.
- Option B: Compact with dedicated KV cache + capability vault (small feature pack) — slightly higher than A but safer for latency.
- Rollback: can we prepare a pinned model variant (Core-compat) and an autoswitch policy? Need ops input.

Can you put numbers on A vs B (list monthly delta, one-time migration credit) and confirm what our rollback SLA looks like? Also include a sample SOW stub and a pricing spreadsheet we can attach.

I'll draft a customer-facing message once you confirm numbers.

—Kim
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-23T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exploring a lower-cost plan + keep X features

Kim — good summary. Attached a quick grid (Attachment: pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (xlsx)) with the two scenarios and cost deltas. Highlights:

- Option A (Compact + caching add-on): ~22% cost reduction vs current committed spend. Includes prefix cache add-on (1x small cache pool). Estimated p95 risk: moderate — depends on request shape.
- Option B (Compact + dedicated KV cache + route-tracing pack): ~12% cost reduction. Much lower p95 risk and fewer manual ops.

Concession idea: 1 month credit (up to $10k) for migration + 3 migration hours of engineering assistance. If they ask for more, we can escalate.

Rollback: We can pre-provision a Core-compat model variant and enable an autoswitch policy that flips to dedicated capacity for 10 minutes on sustained p95 breaches. Ops will need a short playbook; I flagged this with infra.

I also exported a one-page option summary (Attachment: altomed_option_summary.pdf (pdf)) you can send. If this looks right I’ll generate final pricing_grid_final.xlsx and SOW draft.

—Ben
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: David Liao <david.liao@altomed.com>, procurement@altomed.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-23T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Altomed plan options and next steps

David — thanks for outlining the ask. We ran two practical pathways and attached a short summary (altomed_option_summary.pdf). TL;DR:

- Option A: Move to Compact + Prefix Caching add-on. Best cost down (~22%), minimal contract change. Tradeoff: p95 risk is elevated for bursty flows; recommended for non-critical user flows.
- Option B: Move to Compact + Dedicated KV cache + Tracing pack. Smaller cost savings (~12%) but preserves p95; recommended for user-facing paths.

Concession we can offer: one-month account credit (up to $10k) + 3 hours of migration assistance included. If you need an extra week of embedded help, we can offer that as a paid add-on.

Rollback: We will prepare a pinned Core-compat variant and an automatic fallback policy that routes to dedicated capacity for short bursts. That will let you revert within minutes.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tell us which option (A or B) you prefer.
2) If B, indicate any target p95 headroom you want us to guarantee.
3) If A and you want the extra safety, we can provision a warm fallback for a small incremental cost.

Attaching summary and will follow up with SOW + final pricing if you pick an option. Happy to jump on a 30m call tomorrow.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: David Liao <david.liao@altomed.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@altomed.com
Date: 2028-05-24T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Altomed plan options and next steps

Kimberly — thanks, that’s clear. We want to go with Option B (Compact + Dedicated KV cache + Tracing pack). A few clarifications before we sign:
- Can you make the first 30 days of the dedicated cache support a priority response SLA?
- We’d like a 10% credit to the first month’s invoice (noting we’re already reducing spend by moving tiers).
- Procurement also asked whether the SOW can call out a 45-day rollback window post-migration for any unexpected regressions.

If you can accept the 10% month-1 credit and confirm the 45-day rollback window as a contractual checkpoint, we’ll proceed and loop legal for the SOW.

David
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: David Liao <david.liao@altomed.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-24T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Altomed plan options and next steps — concession approval and SOW

David — we can confirm the requested items.

Approved concessions:
- 10% credit applied to the first month invoice (deal ALT-3245).
- Priority response SLA for dedicated cache during the first 30 days (documented in SOW).
- 45-day rollback checkpoint will be included as a contractual review period post-migration.

Attached: Altomed_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW stub) and pricing_grid_final.xlsx (finalized numbers). DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/Altomed/SOW/ALT-3245

Kim — please send the SOW to legal@altomed.com and procurement, and coordinate the migration window. Ben — flag infra/ops to prepare the pinned variant and the autoswitch policy; let me know if you need an escalation exception.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to a smooth migration.

—Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
